title: Hadrosaurus foulkii
body:
Hadrosaurus foulkii stood in Dinosaur Hall as the first mounted dinosaur skeleton anywhere, first mounted in 1868. Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins built that mount, the first to show a dinosaur standing on two legs.

The bones were first noticed in 1838 by John Estaugh Hopkins in a marl pit in Haddonfield, New Jersey. William Parker Foulke excavated the skeleton in 1858, and Joseph Leidy of the Academy described it. Crowds grew so large after the mount went up that the Academy began charging admission.

The cast mount was built for a 2008 exhibit, stored in 2020, and returned to the floor on July 16, 2025. The original fossil bones are kept in the Academy's vertebrate paleontology collection. Collections manager Ned Gilmore said in 2025, "Hadrosaurus foulkii, or Haddy, is a bit of a local celebrity."
tenure: Mounted in 1868, the first mounted dinosaur skeleton anywhere. The current cast mount was built for a 2008 exhibit, stored in 2020, and returned to the floor on July 16, 2025.
fun_facts: Hadrosaurus foulkii has been the New Jersey state dinosaur since 1991.
